title: Phase-fusion prefill/decode harmonizer for mixed-sku MIG fleets
creator: Ayesha Gupta
description: Goal: Reduce tail latency and per-token jitter caused by phase mismatches between prefill and decode scheduling on mixed-MIG, mixed-SKU GPU hosts (H100/L40S/A10). Background: we observe recurring latency spikes when concurrent warmup-prefill batches run on slices that have different preferred clock governors; decode bursts then contend and trigger reactive clock changes that increase latency for short-running requests. Hypothesis: by detecting per-slice preferred kernel and clock phase and intentionally fusing prefill and decode scheduling phases (phase-fusion) we can reduce clock transitions, improve kernel cache hit rate, and lower P99 latency with minimal throughput regression. This ticket implements a harmonizer that 1) records per-slice kernel/clock fingerprint on warmup, 2) delays and co-schedules short-decoding requests to align with warmed slices (micro-slot alignment), and 3) exposes a lightweight policy for canary rollout and fallback to existing scheduler if headroom is insufficient.
acceptance_criteria: P99 latency for <1k token requests on mixed-MIG hosts decreases by >= 12% in bench workloads
No more than 3% throughput regression on long-running buffers (>4k tokens) under steady load
Telemetry shows reduction in clock-transition events per minute on targeted hosts by >= 40%
Feature gate + rollout toggle implemented in runtime and console route-level controls
Automated integration test that injects synthetic MIG slice heterogeneity and validates fallbacks
implementation_notes: Plan: 1) Add lightweight per-slice fingerprinting (kernel_name, preferred_clock_range, recent_token_density) emitted to ephemeral telemetry. 2) Extend prefill scheduler with a micro-slot allocator that can hold short decode worklets for up to 8ms to allow co-location with a warmed slice. 3) Kernel selector to use a two-stage ranking: prefer warmed kernel candidates first, then fall back to cost-optimal kernel. 4) Clock policy: advise clock governor but do NOT force; use polite 'nudge' via preferred_clock hints to hypervisor layer. 5) Expose knobs: micro_slot_ms, min_warm_kernel_hit_rate, max_hold_queue_depth. Trade-offs: holding decode worklets increases tail latency for some requests if micro-slot is missed; we keep hold window small (<=8ms) and allow bypass for high-priority requests. This avoids global throughput stalls. Implementation will be in runtime/scheduler with feature-flag ENV PREFILL_PHASE_FUSION.
testing_plan: Unit tests for scheduler path + kernel ranking, end-to-end bench runs in staging with mixed H100/L40S/A10 fleet. Create synthetic workload generator that alternates short chat messages and long prefill-heavy batches. Run canary on 5% of hosts in cluster-phi with detailed telemetry collection. Checkpoint metrics to compare pre/post: P50/P95/P99 latencies, clock-transition counts, kernel-warm-hit-rate, throughput. Postmortem template created in Confluence linked below for any regressions.
telemetry_queries: SELECT host_id, slice_id, count(*) AS transitions FROM hw_clock_events WHERE ts > now() - interval '1 hour' GROUP BY host_id, slice_id ORDER BY transitions DESC LIMIT 50;
SELECT model, slice_pref_kernel, avg(token_latency_ms) FROM request_traces WHERE phase IN ('prefill','decode') AND deployed='canary' GROUP BY model, slice_pref_kernel;

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Micro-slot holding could increase latency for time-sensitive requests. Mitigation: Bypass rule for requests with priority flag and hard cap on hold window.
Risk: Kernel-fingerprint noise may mislead ranking on cold hosts. Mitigation: Use exponential decay and require min_samples=5 before using fingerprint for ranking.
Risk: Clock nudging may conflict with hypervisor policies. Mitigation: Consult infra team and implement as advisory hints only; add telemetry to detect forced adjustments.
Risk: Unexpected throughput regression on long sequences. Mitigation: Canary on low-traffic pods and compare throughput metrics; feature disabled if regression >3%
notes_for_reviewers: Focus review on scheduler micro-slot allocation correctness, kernel ranking stability under noisy telemetry, and the safe default values for micro_slot_ms and min_samples. We aim for low-risk opt-in canary rollout behind a runtime feature flag. Perf bench scripts are in drive folder; please run on staging fleet before merging.
